extracted.intended_audience: industrial property offices, international depositary authorities, depositors, patent attorneys and WIPO/administrative officials
extracted.subtask_description: Legal/regulatory requirements and practical rules under the Budapest Treaty and its Regulations for depositing microorganisms for patent procedure, for qualifying and operating International Depositary Authorities (IDAs), issuing receipts/viability statements, furnishing samples, fees, publication and related administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and Effect of the Deposit of Microorganisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting States which allow or require deposit of microorganisms for patent procedure shall recognize, for such purposes, the deposit of a microorganism with any international depositary authority; recognition includes the fact and date of deposit and that furnished sample is a sample of the deposited microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting States may require a copy of the receipt issued by the IDA. As far as matters regulated in the Treaty and Regulations are concerned, no Contracting State may require compliance with requirements different from or additional to those provided in the Treaty and Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to Make a New Deposit (when samples cannot be furnished)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an IDA cannot furnish samples (e.g., microorganism no longer viable or export/import prevented), the authority must notify the depositor and the depositor has the right to make a new deposit (subject to conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New deposit should be made with original IDA unless that authority lost status or discontinued functions; depositor must sign a statement alleging the new deposit is the same microorganism; if allegation contested, burden of proof governed by applicable law; if viability of original indicated and new deposit made within three months after notification (or within other publication-based time limits), the new deposit is treated as if made on original deposit date. Right to new deposit does not exist if microorganism has been validly transferred to another IDA that can furnish samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export and Import Restrictions (limitation on effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State recognizes that export/import restrictions on certain microorganisms deposited under the Treaty should apply only where necessary for national security or dangers to health or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a policy limitation: restrictions may be applied but only for those narrow reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and Assurance Requirement for IDA Status
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as an IDA, a depositary institution must be located on the territory of a Contracting State and must benefit from assurances furnished by that State (or by an intergovernmental industrial property organization where applicable) that it complies and will continue to comply with Article 6(2) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurances must be communicated in the declaration under Article 7; if an intergovernmental organization furnishes assurances the institution must be on territory of a member State of that organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Continuous Existence
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must have a continuous existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity is a prerequisite of the status; further procedural measures are provided in the Regulations for discontinuance or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Necessary Staff and Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must have the necessary staff and facilities, as prescribed in the Regulations, to perform its scientific and administrative tasks under the Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.2 specifies that staff and facilities must enable storage that keeps microorganisms viable and uncontaminated and provide sufficient safety measures to minimize loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Impartiality and Objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must be impartial and objective in its operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality means availability to any depositor under the same conditions; IDAs cannot discriminate among depositors based on nationality or residence (see Rule 12.1(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Availability to Any Depositor Under Same Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must be available for the purposes of deposit to any depositor under the same conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports non-discrimination in acceptance and fees; any conditions or limitations must have been specified in the assurances/communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Acceptance, Viability Examination and Storage of Certain Kinds of Microorganisms
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must accept for deposit any or certain kinds of microorganisms, examine their viability and store them, as prescribed in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDA's declaration may specify kinds it will accept; extensions to the list of kinds are possible under Rule 3.3. IDAs must examine viability (Rule 10) and store appropriately (Rule 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Issuance of Receipt and Viability Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must issue a receipt to the depositor and any required viability statement, as prescribed in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 7 details form, languages, signature and contents of receipts (original, new deposit, transfers). Rule 10 sets out viability test and contents of viability statements and when issuance is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Secrecy Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must comply with the requirement of secrecy in respect of deposited microorganisms, as prescribed in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9.2 and other provisions set out secrecy obligations and the limited circumstances (e.g., furnishing samples to entitled parties) under which information or samples may be disclosed; disclosure obligations to depositor upon furnishing of samples (Rule 11.4(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA: Furnishing of Samples (must be expeditious and proper)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must furnish samples of deposited microorganisms under the conditions and in conformity with the procedure prescribed in the Regulations, and must do so in an expeditious and proper manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 2.3 requires expeditious/proper furnishing. Rules 11.1–11.5 prescribe which parties may obtain samples, required declarations, forms, language and fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of IDA Status — Communication Content
rubrics_metrics.description: A depositary institution acquires IDA status by written communication from the Contracting State (or intergovernmental organization) to the Director General including assurances under Article 6(2) and information as provided in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 3.1 requires the communication to indicate name/address of the institution, detailed information on capacity to comply with Article 6(2) (legal status, scientific standing, staff and facilities), kinds of microorganisms to be accepted (if limited), fees to be charged, official languages, and, where applicable, desired effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and Publication of Communication (acquisition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the communication complies with Article 7(1) and Rule 3.1, the Director General shall promptly notify all Contracting States and intergovernmental industrial property organizations and the International Bureau shall promptly publish the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status is acquired from date of publication or the later date indicated in the communication (Article 7(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination or Limitation of IDA Status — Grounds and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting State or intergovernmental industrial property organization may request termination or limitation of an IDA's status on grounds of non-compliance with Article 6 requirements; procedures and notice requirements apply and Assembly decision with two-thirds majority is required for a finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before making a request the reasons must be notified so appropriate corrective action can be taken within six months. Details of procedure are provided in the Regulations (Article 8 and Rule 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defaults by the IDA — Discontinuance and Refusal Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide measures to be taken where an IDA discontinues (temporarily or definitively) performance of its functions or refuses to accept kinds of microorganisms it should accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5 sets out procedures and consequences for discontinuance or refusal, and Rule 4 addresses requests for termination/limitation and their processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Deposit — Requirements and Acceptance Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Original deposit must follow Rules governing making the original deposit, including documentation, acceptance procedure and issuance of a receipt with specific contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6.1–6.4 specify acceptance criteria, required information from depositor, any required tests, and procedural steps for acceptance and recording; Rule 7 then governs receipt form and contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt — Form, Languages, Signature and Contents (original deposit)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA shall issue a receipt for the original deposit; the receipt must follow prescribed form, languages and signature rules and include specified contents (e.g., accession number, date, name/address of depositor, scientific description if supplied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 7.1–7.3 detail: form; languages; signature/seal equivalence (Rule 1.3); contents required for original deposit (identity of deposit, accession number, dates, scientific description or indication that it was not furnished), and communication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt — Contents in Case of New Deposit or Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipts for new deposits or transfers must state specific items including most recent relevant dates and accession number and refer to the original deposit where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 7.4–7.5 set out the contents for new-deposit receipts (including depositor's allegation of sameness), for transfers, and requirements on dating and accession numbering; receipts must be in compliant form/language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication / Later Indication or Amendment of Scientific Description and Taxonomic Designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors may later indicate or amend scientific descriptions and/or proposed taxonomic designations; IDAs must record and, where relevant, attest to such later indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 8.1–8.2 specify the communication procedure and attestation requirements when scientific description or taxonomic designation is later provided or amended; Rule 7.6 addresses communication of such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage of Microorganisms — Duration of Storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules specify the duration of storage of deposited microorganisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9.1 prescribes duration (storage for the whole duration provided in Rule 9.1 — typically for purposes of patent procedure) and Rule 9.2 prescribes secrecy obligations during storage; storage and retention obligations are tied to Treaty/regulation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy of Deposited Microorganisms
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs must maintain secrecy regarding deposited microorganisms subject to the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9.2 and related provisions define secrecy, and Rules 11.1–11.4 define the limited authorized circumstances under which samples or information may be furnished and the required safeguards and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability Test and Viability Statement — Obligation to Test
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs are obligated to perform viability tests and issue viability statements as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 10.1 requires testing; Rule 10.2 prescribes contents of viability statements, the reference to most recent test, form/language/signature rules, and that issuance to depositors or upon request by industrial property offices may be free of charge while other requests may be subject to fees (Rule 10.2(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples to Interested Industrial Property Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA shall furnish a sample of any deposited microorganism to an industrial property office of any Contracting State or organization upon request accompanied by a declaration that an application referring to the deposit has been filed or that the application/patent involves the microorganism and that the sample is needed for patent procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11.1 requires the request to state that the application is pending or led to grant and that the sample and accompanying information will be used only for the patent procedure; furnishing to offices is free of charge (Rule 11.4(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples to Depositor or Authorized Party
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA shall furnish a sample to the depositor on request, or to an authorized party on request if accompanied by a depositor's declaration authorizing the furnishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11.2 governs furnishing to depositor/authorized party and requires a depositor's authorization for third parties; fees for furnishing to parties other than industrial property offices are chargeable subject to Rule 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples to Parties Legally Entitled (Certified Party)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA shall furnish a sample to a 'certified party' on request if the request is made on a form whose contents are fixed by the Assembly and is certified by the industrial property office that an application/patent referring to the deposit exists and that the certified party has a legal right to a sample under the law governing patent procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11.3 details required certifications including publication status and existence of legal right; where accession numbers have been communicated by offices the IDA can furnish samples on that basis without further certification (Rule 11.3(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Rules for Requests, Declarations and Certifications (language, form, contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests/declarations/certifications under Rules 11.1–11.3 must meet common requirements on language, form, signature, dating and contents (name/address, accession number, application/patent details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11.4 prescribes acceptable languages (English/French/Russian/Spanish in certain cases), that documents be in writing, signed and dated, and sets out the specific items each request must contain; containers for samples must be marked with accession number and accompanied by receipt and hazard information; depositors must be notified when samples furnished to others; fees rules apply (free for offices; fees for other parties subject to Rule 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes When Applying Rules to International (PCT) Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application was filed as an international application under the PCT, references to filing with an industrial property office are to be treated as references to the designation of a Contracting State in the international application; certification of publication may be certification of international publication or of publication by the office as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11.5 adapts Rules 11.1 and 11.3 for PCT international applications to ensure operability with PCT procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — Kinds, Amounts and Non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs may charge fees for storage, attestation (Rule 8.2), issuance of viability statements (subject to Rule 10.2(e)), furnishing of samples (subject to Rule 11.4(h)), and communication of information under Rule 7.6; storage fee covers whole duration of storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 12.1 lists fee categories. Rule 12.1(c) requires that fee amounts not vary based on nationality or residence of depositor or requesting party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in Fees — Notification, Publication and Effective Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change in fees charged by an IDA shall be notified to the Director General by the Contracting State or intergovernmental organization which made the declaration; the Director General shall notify and publish changes and their effective dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 12.2(c) provides that increases or changes with no indicated date apply from the thirtieth day following publication by the International Bureau unless another effective date was specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time Limits (years, months, days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for computing time periods expressed in years, months or days: computation starts on day following event; expiration rules for matching days in later months/years and last-day fallback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 12bis.1–12bis.3 set precise counting rules (e.g., if same-numbered day doesn't exist in subsequent month, period expires on last day of that month).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication by the International Bureau — Form and Required Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications by the International Bureau may be on paper or electronic form. At least once a year an up-to-date list of IDAs shall be published indicating kinds of microorganisms accepted and fees; prompt publication of acquisitions, terminations, extensions, discontinuances/refusals, fee changes and requirements is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 13.1–13.2 define publication frequency and which events must be published promptly after occurrence (e.g., acquisition/termination of IDA status, discontinuance of functions, fee changes, Rule 6.3(b) requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly — Composition, Powers, Quorum and Voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assembly consists of Contracting States each with one delegate (one vote); it deals with maintenance and development of the Union, exercises rights/tasks under Treaty, approves Director General reports, establishes committees and may admit observers; quorum is one-half of Contracting States and decisions generally require a majority of votes cast subject to specified supermajorities for certain matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10 sets rules on representation, observer admission, powers, voting by correspondence if no quorum (Article 10(5)(b)), and special majority thresholds for specific decisions (e.g., Article 8(1)(c) two-thirds; Article 14 requires four-fifths or three-fourths for certain amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations — Scope, Adoption and Supremacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide rules concerning matters expressly referred to in the Treaty, administrative requirements and details for implementation; the Assembly may amend Regulations; in case of conflict Treaty provisions prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 12 explains scope and adoption; amendment of Regulations generally requires two-thirds vote, but amendments about furnishing of samples require that no Contracting State vote against (Article 12(4)(b)). Publication and annexed Regulations are adopted with Treaty (Rule references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Dates and Notifications for Treaty Actions (signatures, entry into force, denunciation, communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treaty sets specific timing rules for entry into force, denunciation effects, effectiveness of communications (e.g., acquisition of IDA status by publication/date), and the Director General's notification obligations for signatures, ratifications, declarations, communications, acceptances and denunciations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 15–20 and Rules 3/7/12/13 detail deposit of instruments, three-month entry-after-deposit rules (Article 16), denunciation effective two years after notification (Article 17), communications/publication rules for IDA status (Article 7), and Article 20 enumerates notifications the Director General must send/publish (items i–ix).
